findings.description: Typed projection pairing resolves the vendor counterpart by name heuristics (alias table, exact name, name.removesuffix("Schema"), and for unions the branch with the largest property-name overlap at line 418). When no candidate resolves, the root is silently skipped rather than raising. The attempt-02 required fix had two parts; the first (an explicit committed mapping asserted against the heuristic) is now implemented in contracts/compatibility/g25/projection-bindings.json and tools/g25_fixtures.py:276-277, so a renamed vendor root that drops or re-pairs a field fails the gate with "Reviewed legacy/vendor projection bindings changed". The second part - raising on an unpaired root - is still not implemented, so a future vendor rename that removes a pairing is detected only indirectly, through the 55-row ledger diff, and a rename that produces no field additions at all would not be surfaced.
findings.required_fix: In tools/red_team_dataplane.py:423-426, raise instead of silently continuing when a legacy root resolves no vendor candidate (allowing an explicitly recorded no-counterpart list if some roots legitimately have none), and add a negative test alongside tools/test_g25_generation.py:316-345 proving an unresolvable root fails generation.

findings.description: For models carrying vendor projections, the serializer's KNOWN list deliberately excludes projection wire names, so an extension key equal to a projection field is accepted; when the typed projection is also set, the extension value is skipped at generated.rs serialization (generate_models.py:502-506) and silently dropped, while a baseline-field collision still errors. This cannot arise from a wire document (a successful typed decode removes the key from the raw map), so it only affects callers who use the builder/extension API on the five request-reachable projection models (14 fields), and the behavior is documented at docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:17 and asserted intentionally at crates/scm-sdk/tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs:536-538. It remains a silent caller-side data loss with no diagnostic, unlike every other collision in this crate.
findings.required_fix: Either reject the collision (serialize_map returning an error, or a check in the generated builder's build()) for projection wire keys when the typed field is set, or add an explicit public accessor/doc comment on the generated projection fields stating that setting them discards a same-key extension; cover the chosen behavior with a test next to g25_response_compatibility.rs:522.

findings.description: The remote CI contracts-and-package job still runs tools/check_phase.py --phase 17 --verification-only --contracts-only, whose command set is tools/check_phase.py:ci_commands_for(17) derived from the frozen phase-17 list. That list predates G25, so none of the new guards (g25_audit/g25_fixtures/g25_report --check, tools/g25-oracle.mts, the tsc type-check, and the test_g25*.py suites) execute in CI; they are currently enforced only by the local phase-19 gate. The Rust matrix does execute the new Rust regressions on both compilers, including the added red-team-json-unification combination (.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:90, docs/CI.md:4 documenting 49 jobs, guarded by the passing tools/test_ci.py). The deferral is deliberate and recorded in docs/phase-status.json:4085, and the plan assigns CI wiring to phase 20, so this is a residual gap rather than a phase-19 scope miss.
findings.required_fix: In phase 20, switch the CI contracts job to a G25-scoped verification-only command set that includes the g25 tool --check runs, the oracle and its tsc check, and the test_g25*.py suites, while preserving the historical phase-12/17 command lists for their own records; extend tools/test_ci.py to assert the new job's command list contains those guards.
